entities.summary:
Salome of Poland, also known as Salome of Cracow or Blessed Salome, was a Polish princess born into the royal family of the Piast dynasty in the late 12th century. She became the Queen of Galicia from 1215 to 1219 through her marriage to King Coloman of Galicia.

In 1219, Salome's husband died without a male heir, and she was succeeded by her brother, Henry II the Pious, who ruled Galicia until his death in 1241. Salome's legacy as a queen and a devoted wife has endured, with her feast day still celebrated in Poland and Ukraine.

Salome's significance in the history of Eastern Europe lies in her role as a symbol of the Piast dynasty's influence and her contributions to the cultural and religious development of the region. Her story serves as a testament to the strong female figures who shaped the course of history in medieval Eastern Europe.

Salome's impact on the region can still be seen in the many churches and monasteries she founded, including the Church of the Assumption in Cracow, which remains one of the city's most famous landmarks.

The legacy of Salome of Poland continues to inspire historians and scholars, who see her as a key figure in the history of medieval Eastern Europe. Her story serves as a reminder of the enduring power of women in shaping the course of history.
